projects.name: Lumen Health
projects.description: A clinical intelligence platform that turns patient data into real-time care decisions.
projects.overview:
Lumen Health runs triage for a network of outpatient clinics in the US. Their care teams were reading the same patient history three times — once in the EHR, once in a spreadsheet, once in a handover call — before anyone could decide who needed to be seen first.

We rebuilt that flow into a single clinical intelligence surface: every signal a clinician needs, ranked, on one screen.
projects.challenge: Patient data lived across four systems with no shared identity, and anything touching it had to stay HIPAA-compliant. The old dashboard took eleven seconds to load a single patient — long enough that staff had stopped using it.
projects.solution:
A Next.js app backed by Supabase with row-level security, an ingestion pipeline that normalises records into one patient timeline, and an OpenAI-powered summariser that drafts a triage note a clinician can accept or edit in one click.

Everything is audited, reversible, and degrades to the raw record when the model is unsure.
projects.outcome: Triage decisions that used to take just under four minutes now take ninety seconds, and the platform has become the first screen the care team opens each morning.
projects.quote: We stopped arguing about the data and started acting on it. That shift is worth more than the software.

projects.name: Vaultline
projects.description: Treasury & payments infrastructure moving eight figures monthly with zero downtime.
projects.overview: Vaultline moves treasury and payments for mid-market businesses across the UK and EU. When we came in they were processing real money on a codebase built for a pilot — one region, one currency, one very nervous engineer.
projects.challenge: Ledger writes and payment calls shared the same transaction, so a slow provider could lock the books. Reconciliation was manual, and a single failed webhook could leave a balance wrong for hours.
projects.solution:
We split the system into an append-only ledger and an idempotent payments layer talking over a queue, with Stripe as one provider behind a common interface rather than the interface itself.

Every movement is double-entry, every external call is replayable, and reconciliation runs continuously instead of at month end.
projects.outcome: The platform has processed over $40M with zero unplanned downtime, and adding a new payment provider is now a week of work instead of a quarter.
projects.quote: The first month after launch was the quietest month our finance team has ever had.

projects.name: Fieldstone
projects.description: An end-to-end real estate operating system for listings, tours and closings.
projects.overview: Fieldstone is a real estate operating system for a Dubai brokerage running listings, viewings and closings across two emirates — previously across WhatsApp, a shared drive and a whiteboard.
projects.challenge: Agents work from their phones, often with patchy signal between viewings. Anything that needed a stable connection to be useful simply wouldn't get used, and leads went cold while paperwork sat in someone's inbox.
projects.solution:
A React Native app with an offline-first cache that syncs when signal returns, on top of a Laravel platform handling listings, documents and closing workflows.

Leads route to whoever is actually nearby and free, and every viewing writes back to the same timeline the closing team works from.
projects.outcome: Lead-to-viewing conversion improved 3.4×, and the brokerage retired both the shared drive and the whiteboard within the first month.
projects.quote: Our agents stopped asking where something was. It is all just there, on the phone, in the car, between viewings.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Tekoovi builds software for founders and teams who take their data seriously — so we hold ourselves to the same standard. This policy explains what we collect, why we collect it, and the control you keep over it.

privacyClauses.heading: Who we are
privacyClauses.body:
Tekoovi is a digital product studio that designs and engineers websites, SaaS platforms, AI solutions and mobile apps. This policy covers tekoovi.com and any enquiry you send us through it.

For anything privacy-related, including the requests described below, write to hello@tekoovi.com and a person will answer you.

privacyClauses.heading: Information we collect
privacyClauses.body:
We only collect what we actually need to reply to you and keep the site working:

- Details you send us. Your name, email address, company and whatever you write in an enquiry or discovery-call booking.
- Technical data. IP address, browser type, device and referring page, logged automatically when you visit.
- Usage data. Which pages you open and how long you stay, so we can tell which work is worth showing.

We do not ask for payment card numbers on this site, and we do not collect special-category data such as health or biometric information.

privacyClauses.heading: How we use it
privacyClauses.body:
Your information is used to respond to your enquiry, prepare and deliver proposals, run projects we have agreed with you, keep the site secure, and — only if you have opted in — send you occasional studio updates.

We do not sell your data. We do not share it with advertisers, and we do not use it to build profiles for anyone else's marketing.

privacyClauses.heading: Legal basis for processing
privacyClauses.body:
Where UK and EU data protection law applies, we rely on: your consent for optional marketing; performance of a contract when we are working on your project; and our legitimate interests in replying to enquiries, securing our site and improving our services.

Where we rely on consent, you can withdraw it at any time without affecting anything done before you withdrew it.

privacyClauses.heading: Cookies and analytics
privacyClauses.body:
We use a small number of essential cookies to make the site function, and privacy-respecting analytics to understand traffic in aggregate.

You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Essential cookies aside, nothing on this site tracks you across other websites.

privacyClauses.heading: Service providers we rely on
privacyClauses.body:
Running a studio means using a handful of trusted platforms — hosting, email, scheduling and analytics providers — and some of them process data on our behalf.

Each one is bound by a contract that limits them to our instructions, and we share only the minimum they need to do their job.

privacyClauses.heading: International transfers
privacyClauses.body:
We work with clients across 18 countries, so your information may be processed outside the country you live in.

When data moves across borders we make sure an appropriate safeguard is in place, such as standard contractual clauses or an adequacy decision covering the receiving country.

privacyClauses.heading: How long we keep it
privacyClauses.body:
Enquiries that do not turn into projects are deleted within 24 months. Project records are kept for the length of the engagement and for 7 years afterwards, where tax and accounting rules require it.

Server logs are rotated within 90 days. When a retention period ends, data is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.

privacyClauses.heading: How we protect it
privacyClauses.body:
Traffic to this site is encrypted in transit with TLS. Access to client data is limited to the people working on your engagement, protected by multi-factor authentication and reviewed regularly.

No system is perfectly secure, but if a breach ever affects your rights we will notify you and the relevant regulator without undue delay.

privacyClauses.heading: Your rights
privacyClauses.body:
Depending on where you live, you can ask us to:

- Give you a copy of the information we hold about you.
- Correct anything inaccurate or incomplete.
- Delete your data where we have no continuing reason to keep it.
- Restrict or object to how we process it, including direct marketing.
- Send your data to another provider in a portable format.

Email hello@tekoovi.com and we will respond within 30 days. You are also free to complain to your local data protection authority.

privacyClauses.heading: Children
privacyClauses.body: This site is aimed at businesses and is not directed at children under 16. We do not knowingly collect their information, and we delete it promptly if we discover we have.

privacyClauses.heading: Changes to this policy
privacyClauses.body: When this policy changes we update the date at the top of the page. If a change materially affects your rights, we will tell you directly rather than expecting you to notice.

blogs.title: Shipping AI features without breaking trust
blogs.author: Tekoovi Team
blogs.excerpt: How we wire LLMs into products with guardrails, evals and graceful fallbacks — so the magic never becomes a liability.
blogs.content:
Everyone wants an AI feature. Fewer teams think about what happens when the model is confidently wrong in front of a paying customer.

We start every AI build with an eval harness — a fixed set of real inputs and expected behaviours. Before a single prompt ships, we know how often it succeeds, and we watch that number like we watch uptime.

Guardrails come next: strict output schemas, retries with backoff, and a deterministic fallback path for when the model is unavailable or off-target. The user should never see a raw stack trace or an empty screen.

The result is AI that feels magical on the good days and simply feels normal on the bad ones — which is exactly the bar for something people rely on.

blogs.title: The design system is the product
blogs.author: Tekoovi Team
blogs.excerpt: Why we invest in tokens, components and motion rules on day one — and how it pays back across every screen you ship after.
blogs.content:
A design system is not a nice-to-have you bolt on later. It is the grammar of the product, and the earlier you write it, the faster everything downstream moves.

We start with tokens — colour, type, spacing, motion — as CSS variables, not hard-coded values. One change updates the whole surface, light and dark, without hunting through files.

Components are built once, accessibly, and reused everywhere. Motion is codified into a small set of easings and durations so the whole app moves with one personality.

The payoff shows up around week three, when new screens take hours instead of days and still look like they belong.

blogs.title: Scaling to a million users from day one
blogs.author: Tekoovi Team
blogs.excerpt: Foundations that hold under load without over-engineering the MVP — the pragmatic middle path we take on every build.
blogs.content:
Premature scaling kills startups as surely as no scaling does. The trick is building foundations that can grow without paying for capacity you don't need yet.

We design the data model and API contracts for the shape of a million users, but we deploy the smallest infrastructure that serves the first thousand. Stateless services, indexed queries and cache-friendly reads mean the same code scales by turning a dial, not by a rewrite.

Observability goes in on day one — logs, traces and a couple of dashboards — so the first sign of strain is a graph, not an outage.

When growth comes, and it does, the system bends instead of breaking.
